en: Points of Controversy Great Fifty-Section Fifth Chapter
The Discussion on Knowledge of Fruition:
Is there knowledge of fruition for a disciple?
Yes, [it is].
Does the disciple manifest the fruit that has been accomplished?
One should not say so… [and so forth]… Does the disciple possess knowledge regarding the fruit?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does a disciple possess the knowledge of the degrees of others’ attainments of the fruits [of the path], the degrees of their faculties, and the degrees of their individuality?
You must not say so … [and so on] … No, indeed.
Is there knowledge of the fruit for a disciple? Yes.
Is there for a disciple the designation of aggregates, the designation of bases, the designation of elements, the designation of truths, the designation of faculties, and the designation of persons?
It should not be said so … [as before] … Is there knowledge of the fruit for a disciple? Yes.
Is the disciple a Conqueror, a Teacher, a Perfectly Enlightened One, all-knowing, all-seeing, the Lord of Dhamma, and one who has the Dhamma as his refuge?
You should not say so… [as before]… Does the disciple possess the knowledge of the fruit?
“Yes,” [you say].

“Is a disciple one who brings about the arising of the unarisen path, who produces the unproduced path, who proclaims the unproclaimed path—one who knows the path, understands the path, and is skilled in the path?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] … .
Is it not to be said that "there is knowledge of the fruit for a disciple"?
Yes, it is.
Is the disciple ignorant?
One should not say so... [etc.
...Therefore, it follows that the disciple possesses knowledge regarding the fruit (phala-ñāṇa)... [etc. ...
The Discussion on Knowledge of Fruition is finished.
The Fifth Chapter.
Its summary verse:

Knowledge of liberation; the knowledge of one in training regarding the state beyond training; knowledge of what is contrary; the knowledge that there is a departure from the fixed course for one who is not yet destined for it;
all knowledge as analytical knowledge (paṭisambhidā); conventional knowledge; knowledge of the penetration of others' minds;
knowledge of the future; knowledge of the present; and the knowledge of the fruit for a disciple.
The Great Fifty.
Its summary verse:
The seven acquisitions, the one who brings [the gift], strength, the householder, the Arahant, and liberation as the fifth.
